rows: Primary node
Coordinates cluster services and jobs.
Core nodes
Run work and hold HDFS blocks; size for storage and interruption tolerance.
Task nodes
Add compute without storing HDFS blocks.
Instance groups
Use one instance type per group.
Instance fleets
Mix eligible instance types with capacity and allocation strategies.
Managed scaling
Both groups and fleets have support in eligible releases; verify the target release.
S3 versus HDFS
S3 is durable lake storage; cluster-local HDFS ends with the cluster.
Glue Catalog
Crawler infers metadata; a catalog entry does not copy or transform data.

title: Redshift, Athena and BI decisions
rows: COPY
Load warehouse data from S3 with appropriate IAM and network paths.
Spectrum
External tables query S3 data through supported catalog and permissions.
WLM
Queue wait and run time diagnose different bottlenecks.
Concurrency scaling
Adds transient capacity for eligible queries; it does not fix inefficient SQL.
Snapshot
Manual and automated retention differ; cross-Region copies require key access and restore testing.
Athena
Partitions, columnar formats, compression and file size reduce scanned bytes.
Federation
Lambda connectors add source, secret, network and spill-bucket considerations.
SPICE
Import enables in-memory queries with refresh lag; direct query depends on source behavior.
Sharing
Published dashboard access and dataset row/column security are separate controls.

title: Inspector coverage and vulnerability lifecycle
rows: EC2 inventory
Agent-based collection uses Systems Manager. Hybrid scanning also uses EBS snapshots for eligible unmanaged instances.
Eligibility
Supported operating systems, inventory freshness, tags, volume/filesystem constraints and permissions determine scan coverage.
Network reachability
EC2 network exposure analysis is distinct from software-package CVE detection.
ECR images
Enhanced scanning assesses supported OS and programming-language packages. Repository filters, ACTIVE images and rescan settings determine eligibility.
Lambda standard
Scans supported function and layer dependencies for package vulnerabilities; function eligibility and supported runtimes apply.
Lambda code
Optional code scanning checks supported application code; standard scanning is a prerequisite.
Lambda encryption
Current Inspector documentation excludes Lambda functions encrypted with customer managed keys; inspect coverage rather than assuming assessment.
Expanded portfolio
The PDF three-resource list is not an exhaustive current portfolio: Inspector Code Security also assesses supported code, dependencies and IaC.
Prioritization
Use finding risk context, exploitability, exposure and workload impact with severity to assign response priority.
Closure
Patch or rebuild, deploy the corrected version, confirm coverage and review the updated finding; document justified exceptions.

title: Config recording, evaluations and remediation
rows: Recorder scope
Record required resource types in every relevant account and Region; check recorder permissions and health.
Resource history
Configuration items, relationships and compliance timelines answer what changed and when.
CloudTrail correlation
Where recorded, API activity can help identify the principal and operation associated with a configuration change.
Managed rules
Use supported AWS-maintained checks; avoid the PDF historical fixed rule count.
Custom rules
Use Custom Lambda rules or Custom Policy rules written in Guard; custom does not mean Lambda-only.
Triggers
Configuration-change and periodic triggers depend on the rule. Supported proactive evaluation assesses supplied properties before deployment.
Enforcement
A compliance result is an evaluation, not an IAM deny. Preventive policy or deployment controls must enforce a gate.
Aggregation
An aggregator provides a central recorded-data view; source recording and rule deployment remain separate configuration tasks.
Remediation role
Configure an appropriate AutomationAssumeRole and supported runbook parameters. Scope permissions to the intended action and resource.
Stale evaluation
Automatic remediation can use an older compliance snapshot, even after a resource becomes compliant; validate live state in the runbook.
Verification
Use retries, bounded failures, exceptions and approval for disruptive actions; re-evaluate and preserve runbook evidence.
Change notifications
A configured Config delivery channel can publish configuration-change notifications to SNS; authorize the delivery path and monitor delivery health.

title: GuardDuty coverage and organization operations
rows: Foundational sources
CloudTrail management events, VPC flow information and DNS signals supply the foundational detector.
Independent source delivery
Your own trail, VPC Flow Log export or DNS log destination is not a prerequisite for GuardDuty foundational analysis; retain your own audit evidence separately.
Detection method
Threat intelligence, statistical/behavioral analysis and machine learning identify suspicious patterns rather than configuration compliance.
S3 and EKS
S3 Protection examines data access events; EKS Protection examines audit activity. These are distinct from malware scanning and runtime events.
RDS and Lambda
RDS Protection examines supported database login activity; Lambda Protection examines network activity.
Runtime Monitoring
Eligible EKS, ECS/Fargate and EC2 resources require security-agent coverage. Agent deployment and health must be managed.
Malware plans
Supported EBS, S3 and AWS Backup malware protection have distinct prerequisites, scope and operational behavior.
Newer protection
Current plans include AI Protection for supported Bedrock/SageMaker activity. Check Region support and enablement for each plan.
Cryptocurrency indicators
Dedicated cryptocurrency-related findings can indicate malicious resource use; confirm whether the activity is expected before containment.
Finding response
EventBridge rules can send notification through SNS or invoke Lambda/workflow targets; detections do not automatically block access.
Delegation
The organization management account establishes trusted access and designates a member administrator. Verify members, Regions and every protection plan.
Cost and trial
Review current per-plan pricing, trial eligibility and usage estimates. Do not treat a historical 30-day trial as a permanent pricing guarantee.

title: Security Hub, CSPM and investigation boundaries
rows: Service distinction
Security Hub prioritizes and responds to correlated issues; Security Hub CSPM evaluates enabled controls and posture.
Config prerequisite
Most AWS CSPM controls rely on Config recording. Both Hub and CSPM use the current service-linked recorder path; CSPM alone requires customer setup.
Regional control
Enable relevant services and required recording in each source account and Region. An aggregation view does not create missing source coverage.
Integration inventory

The source includes GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, Config, IAM Access Analyzer, Systems Manager, Firewall Manager, AWS Health and partner inputs; use the current integration catalog and required product permissions.
Control versus threat
A failed posture control and a detected attack can affect the same resource, but represent different evidence and response priorities.
Administration
Security Hub organization policies and CSPM central configuration have different enablement/configuration behavior.
Finding lifecycle
Preserve source, resource, account, Region, event time, severity, workflow status, owner and evidence references.
Detective graph
Behavior graph visualizations correlate entities and time-based activity using supported CloudTrail, VPC and GuardDuty context.
Investigation scope
A graph is investigative context. Validate expected behavior, affected principals and resources before selecting containment.
Finding format
Security Hub CSPM normalizes findings into ASFF. Supported custom products submit ASFF through BatchImportFindings; arbitrary personal formats are not accepted unchanged.

title: Macie discovery and sensitive-data response
rows: Supported estate
Macie inventories supported S3 general purpose buckets in the enabled Region; it is not a general scanner for every AWS datastore.
Automated discovery
Automated sensitive-data discovery samples eligible objects to provide broad visibility; review coverage and exclusions.
Discovery jobs
Choose bucket/object scope, sampling and one-time or recurring schedule appropriate to the question.
Identifiers
Managed identifiers provide supported built-in detection. Custom data identifiers and allow lists tune relevant matching and exclusions.
Object access
Supported file formats, object size/storage class and encryption affect eligibility. IAM/bucket and KMS key access must permit analysis.
Two finding classes
Bucket-policy/security posture findings differ from findings about sensitive object content such as PII.
Delivery
Use EventBridge and supported integrations to route findings to an owner or controlled response.
Remediation
Apply approved S3/IAM controls to reduce exposure, validate intended access and retain discovery and remediation evidence.

title: Log types, destinations and limitations
rows: ALB and CLB access
Access logs deliver request information to S3 when configured. Grant the required bucket delivery permissions.
NLB access
NLB access logs cover TLS listener requests and deliver to S3; they are not a log of every TCP or UDP flow.
CloudTrail activity
Trails can deliver to S3 and optionally CloudWatch Logs. Select management/data events, accounts and Regions required for the audit.
VPC Flow Logs
Deliver supported flow records to CloudWatch Logs, S3 or Data Firehose. Flow metadata is not packet capture or application payload.
Public DNS queries
Route 53 public hosted-zone query logs go to CloudWatch Logs with the documented us-east-1 setup; cached resolver responses do not produce new authoritative queries.
Resolver queries
Resolver query logging covers the VPC DNS path and supports configured CloudWatch Logs, S3 or Firehose destinations; it is distinct from public hosted-zone logging.
S3 server access
Deliver bucket request access records to a suitable S3 target; delivery is best effort. CloudTrail data events provide a separate audit mechanism.
CloudFront requests
Legacy standard logs deliver to S3; standard logging v2 supports configured S3, CloudWatch Logs or Firehose delivery. Request logging and API activity are different.
Config delivery
Config can deliver history and snapshots to S3 using the delivery-channel configuration; recording and compliance evaluation remain distinct.
Retention and integrity
Set retention, encryption, access controls, key policy and delivery monitoring. Treat raw logs and summarized findings as separate evidence products.

title: Audit, residency, threat modelling and AI controls
rows: Security Lake records
Normalize supported sources to OCSF and store lake data in S3. Custom sources must meet schema and ingestion requirements.
Subscriber access
Lake Formation/query or object-access subscribers receive only authorized source and Region scope; grant and review access deliberately.
Audit Manager
Frameworks map controls to automated and manual evidence; reviewers select evidence and generate assessment reports.
Evidence judgment
Automated collection does not include all operational evidence or certify compliance; human assessment of scope and effectiveness remains necessary.
Artifact reports
Provider reports and agreements support assurance review; select the period and service scope and follow sharing terms.
Residency controls
Review primary data, replicas, backups, logs, service processing, support paths and external processors against allowed jurisdictions.
Region key limitation
aws:RequestedRegion controls the service endpoint called; some actions have cross-Region effects. Add service-specific data movement controls.
Threat model
Identify assets, actors, data flows, entry points and trust boundaries; enumerate threats and assign mitigations, owners, tests and residual-risk decisions.
Access Analyzer
External, internal and unused access require the appropriate analysis capability and scope. Policy validation complements activity evidence.
Response privilege
Validate event fields, separate investigation and remediation roles, scope resources/actions and record approval and verification outcomes.
AI audit scope
CloudTrail event categories differ by Bedrock API; configure required data selectors and protect separately enabled invocation/application logs.
AI control layers
Content guardrails, retrieval-data access, tool authorization, approval and audit evidence address different failure modes; test their combined behavior.

title: Visual media and document precision
rows: Rekognition labels
Objects, scenes, image text, faces and celebrities are separate capabilities; video person tracking has its own path.
Face verification
A similarity result needs a defined threshold, consent and review for high-impact decisions.
Moderation MinConfidence
Labels below MinConfidence are omitted; lower thresholds raise recall but can raise false positives.
Moderation version
Store model version, request parameters and confidence with reviewed decisions.
A2I human loop
Existing customers can use the Rekognition integration with a flow definition, confidence range or sampling; A2I is not open to new customers.
Textract formats
Document analysis can return text, handwriting, form key/value fields and tables; specialized APIs address expense and ID data.
Extraction validation
Compare totals and confidence with original image; route ambiguous fields to authorized review.
Document security
Source PDF/image and derived structured fields need access, encryption, retention and version controls.
Rekognition face and people cases

Face detection/analysis can return supported attributes such as age range and emotions; face search/comparison, celebrity recognition and people counting/tracking solve different questions. Do not infer identity solely from an attribute.
Moderation use cases
Social media, broadcast, advertising and commerce moderation need policy thresholds, review ownership and local regulatory assessment.
Textract document examples
Invoices and financial reports, medical/insurance records, tax forms, IDs and passports are examples; choose forms, tables or specialized APIs according to fields needed.

title: Speech, localization and contact flow
rows: Transcribe ASR
Audio to text; language identification and PII redaction require compatible configuration.
Transcript privacy
Retain source audio and derived text only as required; redacted output does not erase source audio.
Polly lexicon
Map unusual names/acronyms to pronunciation and attach lexicon in SynthesizeSpeech.
Polly SSML
Use supported tags for emphasis, phonemes and prosody; style/engine support varies by voice.
Translate
Text-to-text translation; supported language pairs and custom terminology need review.
Lex intent
Voice ASR and NLU resolve intent/slots; Lambda can fulfill business logic.
Connect integration
Contact flows receive and route calls; Lex interprets caller intent, Lambda invokes business systems.
Fallback
Low-confidence or unhandled requests must have a human or alternate route and accessible prompts.
Transcribe use cases
Customer calls, subtitles/closed captions and searchable media archives all consume transcripts; language identification helps multilingual inputs.
Polly SSML styles
SSML can express emphasis and phonetic pronunciation; breathing, whispering and Newscaster style have voice/engine/Region support differences. Test the selected combination.
Polly lexicon example
A lexicon can map stylized personal names or an acronym such as AWS to the intended pronunciation; attach the uploaded lexicon to the synthesis request.
Translate use cases
Localize website/application content and large text collections; translation accuracy depends on language pair and domain terminology.
Connect cost claim
The PDF states a fixed percentage saving versus a traditional contact center; treat it as historical marketing, compare current usage and telephony pricing instead.

title: Language, clinical text and recommendations
rows: Comprehend language
Language detection identifies source text language before downstream analysis.
Entities/key phrases
Extract names, places, brands, events and key phrases with service confidence.
Sentiment/syntax/topics
Sentiment, token/part-of-speech syntax, and document topic modeling serve different questions.
Comprehend Medical
Clinical notes, discharge summaries, tests and narratives can yield medical entities and relationships.
DetectPHI
Use the dedicated medical API; never treat detection as exhaustive de-identification.
Personalize historical
Interactions, user/item data and S3 ingestion support tailored recommendations.
Personalize real-time
Event integration updates context; recommendations can be served to web/mobile and messaging.
Recommendation evaluation
Measure relevance, cold-start impact, user consent and fairness.
Comprehend customer examples
Email and customer-interaction sentiment can reveal experience trends; topic modeling groups articles/documents but is not a supervised category assignment.
Medical input paths

Physician notes, discharge summaries, test results and case notes can come from protected S3 storage, approved transcription or streaming pipelines; check regional service integration and PHI handling.
Personalize use cases
Product recommendations, personalized ranking/re-ranking and tailored marketing can serve retail and media/entertainment; batch campaigns and real-time API have different delivery paths.
Personalize event API
Record supported real-time interactions with an event tracker/PutEvents, then query a recommender or campaign; avoid implying an S3 batch update is instantaneous.

title: Model training, forecasting and search
rows: SageMaker data split
Keep training and held-out evaluation data separate; avoid leakage.
SageMaker lifecycle
Prepare, train, tune, evaluate, deploy and monitor; batch, asynchronous, serverless and real-time inference have different contracts.
SageMaker Canvas
No-code custom numeric, categorical and time-series predictions are available; verify current Region and pricing.
Forecast availability
Amazon Forecast no longer accepts new customers since 25 July 2024; existing customers continue.
Forecast legacy claims
The PDF’s 50% accuracy and months-to-hours figures are marketing examples, not guaranteed SLOs.
Kendra availability
Amazon Kendra no longer accepts new customers from 30 July 2026; existing customers can continue.
Kendra indexing
Indexes supported document formats/connectors; ranking, freshness and feedback differ from model-generated answers.
New search architecture
Assess Bedrock Knowledge Bases and its retrieval access controls, connector support and answer quality.
SageMaker labeled example
Features such as past experience and study time plus historical labels train a predictor; a new feature vector yields a prediction, not an observed outcome.
Forecast features and scenarios

Historical target time series can pair with related time series such as price, promotion or web traffic and item metadata; demand, financial and resource planning are example uses for existing customers.
Kendra documents and connectors

Existing deployments may index supported text/PDF/HTML/PowerPoint/Word/FAQ content from S3, supported databases, Google Drive, SharePoint, OneDrive or custom sources; verify connector version and authorization.
Kendra relevance controls
Natural-language answers/search ranking can use interaction feedback, freshness and document importance; tune relevance against representative queries and verify source ACLs.

title: Bedrock, retrieval and operational boundaries
rows: Direct inference
Bedrock model invocation does not automatically search internal documents.
Ingestion
Knowledge Base source role, parser, chunking, embeddings, index and sync lifecycle are distinct.
Retrieval
Caller filters and document-level permissions need validation; review connector and KB type support.
Managed versus customer-managed KB
Managed KB handles retrieval infrastructure; customer-managed variant exposes vector-store and ingestion choices.
RAG grounding
Evaluate retrieval relevance and answer faithfulness separately; include source references and an abstain path.
Guardrails
Supported text/chat inference checks input/output; embedding, reranking and image generation models do not support guardrails.
Invocation logging
Disabled by default, per account/Region, with same-account/Region CloudWatch Logs or S3 destination for supported bedrock-runtime calls.
Log sensitivity
Prompts, retrieved text and outputs may contain secrets or private data; encrypt, scope access and retain deliberately.
Cost drivers
Indexing, vector storage, retrieval, model input/output, endpoints and transfer can each contribute.
Permission gates
Model access, KB ingestion role, data-store access, KMS and end-user authorization are separate.

title: Agent orchestration and action contracts
rows: InvokeAgent
The agent can classify, choose retrieval or action, request missing inputs, observe results and iterate until response.
Action schema
An action group defines supported parameters and function or API shape; executor validates all input.
Lambda fulfillment
Action-group Lambda requires resource-based permission for Bedrock; Lambda execution role governs downstream APIs.
Return control
InvokeAgent returns invocationInputs and invocationId; app executes only after its own policy and returns result with the same IDs in sessionState.
Session history
Context can influence orchestration but must not become authorization.
Version and alias
Test prepared agent version/alias and permission scope before production invocation.
Retrieval data
A KB supplies answer context; retrieved instructions are untrusted content.

title: AgentCore identity and tool policy
rows: Inbound access
Use appropriate IAM/JWT authorization to identify callers of runtime or gateway.
Outbound access
Credential provider can vend scoped OAuth or API credentials to tool integrations; do not place secrets in prompts.
User versus workload
Separate end-user delegation from machine-to-machine access; retain request origin in audit.
Gateway policy
A configured policy engine can authorize CallTool against caller, tool and context; test default-deny behavior.
Target permissions
Gateway authorization and the downstream target permissions are distinct checks.
Cross-boundary
Verify account, Region and session identity propagation limits before relying on a delegated pattern.
Resource scope
Limit agent, KB, tool and secret ARNs/permissions; avoid universal administrative roles.

title: Content safety and responsible AI
rows: Input/output guardrail
Configure supported content, denied-topic, word and sensitive-information policies; evaluate both directions.
Prompt attack
Treat retrieved documents and tool responses as data; configure filters and enforce independent tool policy.
Automated Reasoning
Policy logic can identify contradictions and assumptions only for modeled variables; it is not prompt-injection defense.
Current limitations
Automated Reasoning checks are English US, non-streaming and limited to modeled policy scope per AWS docs reviewed 2 November 2026.
Fairness and accuracy
Evaluate representative cohorts and edge cases; record failures and affected user groups.
Human escalation
Provide abstention, appeal and ownership for high-impact decisions.
Policy version
Retain configuration/version with test evidence and decision records.

title: Approval, recovery and evidence
rows: Confirmation timing
Obtain approval before invoking a state-changing action; denial must not call executor.
Approval context
Show exact target, parameters, consequence and supporting evidence; protect reviewer authentication.
Callback token
Step Functions task-token workflow pauses until authorized callback or timeout.
Stale approvals
After approval, recheck current resource and policy before side effect; bind approved payload to execution.
Idempotency
Deduplicate retries with business request ID and store execution outcome.
Denial and timeout
Record reject/expired state and route to safe response or escalation without action.
Traces and logs
Agent trace, CloudTrail API events and app approval logs answer different questions; redact sensitive prompts/outputs.
Telemetry defaults
AgentCore service metrics and optional spans/logs vary by resource; explicitly configure destinations where needed.

title: Stack policies and safe updates
rows: DeletionPolicy Delete
Default except documented RDS Snapshot defaults. An S3 bucket must be empty before CloudFormation deletes it.
DeletionPolicy Retain
Retained resource leaves stack management and continues to incur charges.
DeletionPolicy Snapshot
Only supported resource types; EBS, ElastiCache, RDS, Redshift plus current DocumentDB and Neptune clusters are documented examples.
RDS defaults
AWS::RDS::DBCluster and AWS::RDS::DBInstance without DBClusterIdentifier default to Snapshot.
RetainExceptOnCreate
Behaves like Retain except rollback of initial create deletes the just-created resource.
UpdateReplacePolicy
Controls the old physical resource during replacement; DeletionPolicy controls removal/deletion.
Change set
Review replacement/conditions and failure effects; a preview is not deployment proof.
Stack events
Inspect failure reason, rollback state and retained physical IDs after operation.
Drift limits
Only supported resource properties can be compared; manual edits are not prevented.

title: Custom resources and secrets
rows: Lifecycle
Handle Create, Update, Delete and provider callback for the stack request.
Physical ID
Stable identifier enables CloudFormation to correlate updates and deletes.
Retry/idempotency
Timeout and rollback can repeat calls; provider must avoid duplicate side effects.
External systems
Custom resource may call an external/on-premises API or do S3 cleanup when properly scoped.
Secret reference
Use Secrets Manager dynamic reference in supported resource property rather than embed plaintext.
Rotation boundary
Secret rotation and CloudFormation stack update are different operations; validate consumer refresh.
Unsupported locations
Secure dynamic references have documented exclusions such as custom resources and UserData.
SSM SecureString
Use ssm-secure dynamic reference only in supported CloudFormation properties; grant SSM and KMS access.
Versioned references
Pinning a version requires a template update to advance; unversioned value rotation still does not automatically trigger a stack update.
Runtime retrieval
Application role independently needs scoped GetSecretValue or GetParameter and KMS permissions.

title: StackSets and resource import
rows: StackSet regional
Administration resource lives in one Region; instances deploy to chosen account/Region targets.
Permission models
Self-managed uses administrator/execution roles; service-managed integrates Organizations.
Auto deployment
New accounts in target OUs can receive instances when enabled; removal behavior can retain or delete.
Override caveat
Future OU accounts use StackSet default parameters, not old per-account overrides.
Operation preferences
Choose Region order, concurrency and per-Region failure tolerance; inspect partial failure.
Manual import
Template describes entire stack, identifier maps existing resource, each imported item has any valid DeletionPolicy.
Auto-import
Supported type with static custom name, identifier, Retain or RetainExceptOnCreate; no existing stack ownership.
Import isolation
Manual IMPORT change set does not combine unrelated create/delete/property changes.
Post-import
Run drift detection before subsequent updates; verify template and live properties.

title: Service Catalog, SAM and CDK
rows: Catalog product
Approved, versioned provisioned product may use CloudFormation or supported Terraform artifact.
Portfolio
Groups products, grants users access, applies constraints per association.
Launch role
Service Catalog assumes scoped role for launch/update/termination; user portal permission differs.
SAM declarations
AWS::Serverless::Function, API, SimpleTable and StateMachine are supported examples.
SAM local
sam local invoke/start-api offers local testing; cloud integrations and IAM still require deployed tests.
SAM deployment
SAM transform into CloudFormation; CodeDeploy aliases/alarms/hooks support gradual Lambda shift.
CDK synthesis
Construct application outputs CloudFormation template and deployment assets.
CDK bootstrap
Bootstrap resources/roles may be required for assets/deploy; scope trust and permissions.
CDK languages
Current CDK supports multiple language bindings; inspect synthesized output independent of language.

title: Policy validation and enforcement
rows: Guard rules
Validate JSON/YAML template/change set against modeled requirements such as encrypted S3 or restricted SSH.
Rule tests
Include positive, negative and exception fixtures; preserve validation result with revision.
CI gate
cfn-guard validate can fail automated build when explicitly configured.
Hook targets
Guard/Lambda/custom/Control Tower controls can evaluate configured resources, stack, change set or Cloud Control requests.
Hook mode
Warn mode reports; fail mode blocks affected operation when active and matched.
Control scope
Filters, resource types, account/Region activation and permissions determine actual protection.
Postdeploy check
Config and drift detection observe running state; they are not synonyms for predeployment enforcement.
CDK Aspects
Visit constructs during synthesis; inspect resulting template because the aspect applies only to the scoped CDK tree.
SCP permission ceiling
Organizations SCP limits allowed actions in member accounts; it does not grant IAM access or parse templates.
Config evaluation
Record and evaluate deployed state; remediation is a separate configured action.
